newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT- U.S. T-bonds to hold 109-16 before FOMC.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT- U.S. T-bonds to hold 109-16 before FOMC.

text.p: June U.S. Treasury bond futures will continue to hover above intraday support around 109-16 until the Federal Open Market Committee wraps up its meeting this afternoon, technicians and floor traders said.
Late Tuesday morning, June futures remained moderately lower after an early slide to a session low of 109-13 in jittery, pre-FOMC position-squaring.

Traders and analysts predicted support at 109-16, the session low from May 9, would hold up with most market participants now taken to the sidelines to wait out the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision.

According to the most recent Reuters survey, 21 of 39 primary dealers forecast the Fed would leave the federal funds rate steady at 5.5 percent. The FOMC is expected to announce its decision around 1415 EDT (1815 GMT).

Below the day's lows, the next important level of support for June bonds comes in at 108-30, the May 8 low, while the first serious resistance level is not until 110-16, said Dave Eberhart, market strategist for Optima Investment Research.
At 110-16, Eberhart said, the futures price would be roughly equivalent to a yield on the 30-year cash bond of 6-7/8 percent, an area the market has had trouble breaching in the past.
June bond futures were last trading at 109-19, down 10/32.
Eberhart said he expected the market to extend the upmove that began in early April but more recently has evolved into a wide sideways range of 108-30 to 110-22.
"There doesn't seem to be anything up there that says the market has topped," he said.

Eberhart said a tightening announcement this afternoon would probably be favorable to the market. On the other hand, he warned, a buildup of long positions on the recent upmove could exacerbate any selloff.

Bond floor traders said they were bracing for a potentially sharp move in the wake of the Fed announcement, though they appeared as much divided in their opinion on price direction as on what course of action the Fed would take.

Total open interest in CBOT bond futures has risen sharply as prices have climbed in the past month and a half, reaching a record 602,440 contracts May 14 after sinking to a five-month low of 466,182 open positions April 3, Eberhart noted. As of Monday, open interest in bond futures stood at 561,629 contracts.
"On any kind of break, you'd expect a lot of long liquidation," he said.
